newsitem.title: USA: China to give copper price stability-Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: China to give copper price stability-Macquarie.

text.p: China's huge and growing thirst for copper will increasingly be seen as a stabilizing influence on red metal prices in future and much of the country's extra offtake will have to come from imports, analyst Jim Lennon of Macquarie Equities said Tuesday.

"China is the most critical issue in copper over the next few years - the Chinese market is much bigger than any suspected and will remain a long term bullish influence on prices," Lennon told the American Metal Market magazine copper seminar.
China's copper supplies totalled 1.417 million tonnes in 1996, up nine percent on 1995, with 967,000 tonnes coming from imports of scrap, blister and cathode.
Loosening credit controls will keep Chinese copper consumption prospects bright in 1997, Lennon said.
"A sustained Chinese copper demand growth rate of 10-15 pct a year is really achievable," he added.
If demand increased in China at a "conservative" 12.5 pct a year China's offtake will grow from 1.575 million tonnes this year to 2.243 million tonnes in 2000, he said.
"We estimate that domestic sources can supply only 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes of this extra demand, the rest would come from imports," Lennon said.
"China will need an extra 843,000 tonnes of extra metal by 2000," he said.
But much of this extra copper will be imported and in the form of blister and scrap and other raw material, rather than in cathode as in the past.
